subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as a first-class authorization boundary for triggering OpenClaw agents and tools?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but the requested mode changes Slack access-control semantics and the issue explicitly raises private shared-channel caveats that automation should not decide.

options.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Mode
options.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack, align all Slack admission paths, document Slack Connect caveats, and leave defaults unchanged unless separately approved.

options.title: Reject Private-Channel Boundary
options.body: Keep explicit Slack channel ID allowlists as the only non-open group authorization mode and document private/shared channels as insufficient for this trust decision.

options.title: Defer To Broader Access Design
options.body: Track this under a broader channel authorization design if maintainers want cross-channel semantics instead of a Slack-specific value.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-Scoped Private Mode
recommendation.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack, align all Slack admission paths, document Slack Connect caveats, and leave defaults unchanged unless separately approved.
